notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a full primary research article titled Analytic thinking reduces belief in conspiracy theories, with authors Viren Swami, Martin Voracek, Stefan Stieger, Ulrich S. Tran, Adrian Furnham, and publication line Cognition 133 (2014), 3, pp. 572–585 matching the original reference. It contains Studies 1–4 and references through p. 585. DOI not independently displayed/verified in the supplied header; no network used. No PDF was supplied. Both assigned rows supply identical descriptions and locators. Named Study 4 and p. 10 (printed p. 581) identify a disfluent-font manipulation with two outcomes, generic conspiracist ideation and 7/7 conspiracy beliefs. The supplied scrambled-sentence description instead identifies Study 2 (printed pp. 577–578). Neither row specifies which Study 4 outcome is intended or resolves the study/manipulation conflict. No candidate assigned by row order or numeric matching. Printed candidates (each effect and p belong to the same test): Study 4 generic conspiracist ideation, d = 0.42, t(138) = 2.49, p = .014; Study 4 7/7 conspiracy beliefs, d = 0.34, t(138) = 2.01, p = .046 (sentence spans columns on p. 581); Study 2 post-manipulation belief in conspiracy theories, d = 0.46, t(110) = 2.40, p = .018, p. 578. Study 2 separately reports the condition-by-session interaction F(1, 110) = 5.77, p = .018, g2p = .05. All candidates remain unassigned. No effect conversion or N derivation performed. Unassigned sides and fields are placeholders.
